Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Reproductive-age patient with 2 days of constant, worsening suprapubic pain, increased urinary frequency, and pink urine; mild nausea and subjective feverishness; no dysuria; bowels currently normal; sexually active; on Implanon; LMP ~2–3 weeks ago; last STI screen negative.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Acute uncomplicated cystitis (high likelihood): Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and possible hematuria; systemic features mild; dysuria absent but not required.
  - Urolithiasis (distal ureter/bladder stone) (moderate likelihood): Pink urine and lower abdominal discomfort with frequency; absence of colicky pain or flank pain lowers probability.
  - Early appendicitis (moderate likelihood): Gradual worsening lower abdominal pain with mild nausea and subjective fever; location midline/suprapubic and lack of RLQ migration reduce likelihood.
  - Early pregnancy-related complication including ectopic (low likelihood but must be excluded): Pelvic pain in reproductive-age; on implant reduces risk; no vaginal bleeding reported.
- Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis.
- Management priorities: Empiric antibiotic therapy; confirm not pregnant; safety-net advice and close follow-up; consider further testing if symptoms persist/worsen.

Management Plan

- Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim prescribed; instruction documented as “1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.” Note: clinician initially said “two tablets,” then clarified “one tablet twice daily”—dosing ambiguity noted; patient to follow clarified dosing.
- Symptomatic care: Paracetamol as needed for pain; maintain adequate oral fluids; may try cranberry juice.
- Pregnancy: Advised to complete a pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy-related causes.
- Safety-net: Return or seek urgent care if worsening abdominal pain, persistent fever/hot and sweaty, vomiting, or no improvement within a few days.
- Follow-up: Clinician requested patient to come back in a few days if no improvement or sooner if deterioration.
- Investigations discussed: Initial plan to do tests was discussed; patient opted for empiric treatment first; urinalysis/culture and further evaluation to be considered if not improving.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and possible hematuria with mild systemic features; absence of dysuria does not exclude.
- Urolithiasis (distal ureter or bladder stone) – Moderate likelihood: Hematuria and lower abdominal symptoms could indicate a distal stone; atypical pain character and no flank pain lower probability.
- Early appendicitis – Moderate likelihood: Gradual worsening lower abdominal pain with nausea/subjective fever; lack of RLQ localization and other classic features reduces likelihood.
